subject: Human Body
title: Inflammation: The Alarm Response
description: A quick win: understand Inflammation: The Alarm Response.

hook.text: A paper cut: redness, swelling, heat, pain. That's not damage — it's your immune system mobilizing for war.

buildup.text: Damaged cells release chemical alarms called histamines. Blood vessels dilate, flooding the area with immune cells.

discovery.text: Swelling traps pathogens locally. Heat speeds up enzyme reactions. Pain tells you to protect the area.

twist.text: Chronic inflammation turns destructive. When the alarm never shuts off, it damages healthy tissue over time.

climax.text: Acute inflammation heals. Chronic inflammation harms. The difference between cure and disease is knowing when to stop.

punchline.text: Inflammation saves you short-term. It harms you long-term.

quiz.question: What triggers the inflammatory response?
options: Chemical alarms like histamines from damaged cells
White blood cells detecting invader DNA
